data.body:
## RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1) — NOT A BUG in rebar. Classification: environment-or-config.

Both reported defects are proven, and neither is an in-repo rebar defect. The ticket's
headline premise ("packaged release omits commit_impact.py") is factually disproved.

### Proven root cause (the ImportError)

The host's hourly main-tracking updater `~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh` (host-local,
git-ignored, NOT in this repo) ends every run — publish path AND no-change path — with
`prune_releases()`, which unconditionally `rm -rf`s every release directory other than the
one `current` points at. It does not check whether a process is still executing out of the
directory it deletes.

The published runtime is an EDITABLE install: the release venv's site-packages holds
`_editable_impl_nava_rebar.pth` containing the single line
`<release>/src` — there is no copied `rebar/` package. So a running interpreter resolves
every not-yet-imported rebar module from that release directory at import time.

rebar imports `commit_impact` LAZILY, inside the function body at
`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:283`
(`_check_file_impact_vs_diff` -> `from rebar._engine_support import commit_impact`), which
runs late in a close — after the completion-verifier LLM gate, which routinely takes minutes.

So: a `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` that starts before a prune and is still
running when it fires loses its source tree mid-process. The parent package
`rebar._engine_support` is already in `sys.modules` and survives in memory; the lazy child
import then fails with exactly the reported error.

Timeline (from `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log`), all UTC:
- 17:25:18 — `d83fb4f6` published as current.
- 19:17:37 — next hourly run starts.
- 19:18:01 — `0b851c81` published; `prune_releases` `rm -rf`s `d83fb4f6...98469`.
- 19:55:13 — this ticket filed, quoting a traceback rooted at the now-deleted
  `d83fb4f6...98469` path.

### Discriminating experiments

CONFIRMING — exact-message reproduction. Copied `src/` to a scratch dir, imported
`rebar._engine_support`, `shutil.rmtree()`'d the tree, then ran the lazy import:

    ImportError: cannot import name 'commit_impact' from 'rebar._engine_support'
      (/tmp/rebar-race/src/rebar/_engine_support/__init__.py)

character-for-character the reported failure. Negative control (identical probe, tree left
in place) imports successfully.

REJECTED — "the file is missing from the source at that commit":
`git ls-tree d83fb4f6fdafeafa696238e76eff6933e5674607 src/rebar/_engine_support/` lists
`commit_impact.py` (blob `104d76a8b9283359d54206490cfec3d57ba099d0`). It was there.

REJECTED — "the wheel/build excludes it": built the wheel from origin/main
(`uv build --wheel`) and listed its members — `rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py` is
present (830 members total). `git check-ignore` exits 1 (not ignored). `hatch_build.py`
excludes nothing; it only bakes `_build_info.py`.

REJECTED — "the auto-update installed a build predating the file": the file predates
`d83fb4f6`, and the currently-installed global runtime imports it fine —
`from rebar._engine_support import commit_impact` resolves to
`.../releases/0b851c81.../src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py`.

REJECTED — "this breaks every close with file_impact from a packaged build": disproved by
the two checks above. The failure needs the specific prune-during-run race.

### The "exits 0" half — also not a rebar defect

rebar's exit code is correct. Probe: forced an uncaught ImportError through
`rebar.cli.main()` -> `sys.exit(_main(...))`.
- Bare invocation: traceback on stderr, **exit 1**.
- Same command as `... 2>&1 | tail -20`: shell reports **0** — a pipeline's status is the
  LAST stage's, i.e. `tail`'s.

The reported "[exited with code 0]" is the caller's invocation shape, not rebar. That shape
is in active use on this host; a live process at diagnosis time was literally
`rebar transition e215-... in_progress closed 2>&1 | tail -20`. There is no in-repo defect
to fix and no follow-up ticket is warranted for it.

### Disposition (Phase 2 NOT unlocked — no code change proposed)

1. ImportError: fix belongs in the host-local `~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh`. Options,
   cheapest first: (a) retain the previous release for one cycle instead of pruning
   immediately; (b) skip pruning a release that any live process still references; (c) drop
   the editable install so the release dir stops being a live import root.
2. Exit 0: fix belongs in the caller — `set -o pipefail`, check `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, or don't
   pipe a gated `rebar transition`. Optionally worth a one-line note in contributor guidance,
   since agents in this repo routinely write `rebar ... 2>&1 | tail -N`.

Recommend closing this ticket as not-a-bug / invalid for the rebar repo. Handing that
decision to the operator rather than closing unilaterally.
